title: The string the list forgot
hook: A list claims to hold every endless string of 0s and 1s. Can you catch it out?

knows: that an endless hotel can always fit one more guest (listing things one per room)
what a string of 0s and 1s is
doesNotKnow: that some endless collections cannot be put in a list at all

misconception: Any endless collection can be listed, so a long enough list of 0-1 strings could hold them all.
objective: The learner can explain that flipping the k-th digit of the k-th string builds a string that differs from every row of any list somewhere, so no list holds every endless 0-1 string.

claims.text: A string whose place k is the opposite of row k's place k differs from row k, for every k.
claims.source: By construction: new[k] = 1 - row_k[k] ≠ row_k[k]. Node check on the stage's 8 rows: the new string 01000110 differs from each row at its diagonal place.

claims.text: The stage shows only the first 8 rows and 8 places; the argument is for the whole endless list, where row n differs at place n.
claims.source: The same rule applies to every n; the grid is an illustration. Rows come from mulberry32(1891), an arbitrary seed not chosen for the result (any list gives the same outcome).

claims.text: No list of endless 0-1 strings can hold them all; this is Cantor's diagonal argument.
claims.source: G. Cantor, 'Über eine elementare Frage der Mannigfaltigkeitslehre' (1891). The lesson does not claim more than this about sizes of infinity.

recall.question: To build a 0-1 string missing from a list, which digits do you change?
options: The first digit of every row
Place 1 of row 1, place 2 of row 2, and so on, each flipped
The last digit of the last row
recall.why: Flipping place n of row n makes the new string differ from every row n somewhere, so it cannot be on the list.
